title: blockwise dynamic-rescale INT8/FP8 KV experiments for streaming contexts
creator: Ava Patel
description: Investigate block-wise asymmetric quantization strategies (INT8 and FP8) for KV cache tensors in the streaming inference path. Focus on a dynamic rescale mechanism that updates per-block scaling factors during streaming kv-appends to reduce drift for long contexts while preserving low tail latency. Compare accuracy and token-level latency across representative workloads (chat-like short-turns, long-document streaming up to 16k tokens, and mixed-batch throughput). Provide a recommended default quant profile and a guarded rollout plan (canary + traffic-based fallback) for runtime-1.21.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least 20% median token-latency improvement vs FP32 baseline on single-GPU streaming under target batch sizes for >75% of workloads
Quality degradation <= 2% (relative) on primary eval set for chat workloads; <=4% for long-document holdouts with documented trade-offs
A stable calibration pipeline that reproduces scaling factors within 5% across two independent runs
Proposal for runtime rollout (config flags, telemetry keys, fallback triggers) and an open PR implementing the runtime selection hook
experiment_plan: 1) Implement blockwise asymmetric quantizer for KV tensors with configurable block size (64,128,256) and per-block scale/zero-point for INT8; equivalent mantissa/exponent biased FP8 layout for FP8 path. 2) Calibration harness: (a) offline calibration on sampled representative traces (chat, code, docs); (b) in-situ lightweight calibration that maintains EMA(max_abs) per block during warm-up and freezes after threshold steps; (c) synthetic stress traces for worst-case activations. 3) Run sweep matrix: block sizes x calibration strategy x sequence length {512,2048,8192,16384} x batch sizes {1,4,16}. 4) Collect metrics: per-token latency (p50/p95/p99), end-to-end request latency, perplexity delta, response-quality regressions on eval prompts, SLO violations. 5) Validate on holdout set and run safety checks (nan/inf propagation, drift).
calibration_workflow: Stage A - Offline: sample 200k kv-activation windows from recent production anonymized traces (privacy-preserving sampling), compute per-block statistics (max_abs, mean_abs, 99.9th percentile) and fit asymmetric scales with outlier clipping at 1e-3 fraction. Stage B - Streaming warmup: EMA(max_abs) with alpha=0.02 for first 5k tokens, freeze if variance < 3% over 1k-token window. Stage C - Holdout validation: apply profile to a disjoint set of 10k prompts and compute delta metrics. All artifacts stored in GCS and registered in confluence page for traceability.
results_summary: Preliminary runs on n1-standard GPU instance: FP32 baseline median token latency = 12.4ms, INT8 (block=128, offline calibrated) median = 9.3ms (-25%), FP8 hybrid (block=64, streaming EMA rescale) median = 7.9ms (-36%). p95 improvements consistent but p99 tail shows FP8 tail spikes in mixed-batch runs (p99=68ms vs baseline 55ms) attributed to occasional rescale jitter. Quality: chat eval perplexity delta (vs FP32) = +0.9% for INT8, +1.7% for FP8-hybrid. Long-context (>=8k tokens) shows INT8 sustained quality degradation up to +3.6% perplexity when using offline-only calibration; dynamic-rescale with EMA reduces that to +1.4%. We observed a failure mode where per-block clipping at aggressive thresholds produced token-level artifacts on code-completion prompts in 0.2% of cases — flagged for further mitigation. SLO observations: with FP8-hybrid default config we measured an increase in p99 latency violations by ~40% under adversarial mixed-batch traces; mitigation strategy is to gate FP8 by region/plan or enable local fallback to INT8/FP32 on spike detection.
metrics_collected: nan_inf_events: 0 in 50k requests for INT8; 12 events in FP8-hybrid runs (investigating)
decisions: Adopt blockwise dynamic-rescale (EMA warmup then freeze) as the canonical streaming calibration approach for INT8 to balance long-context quality and latency.
Expose FP8-hybrid as an opt-in experimental profile in runtime-1.21 for non-critical customers and internal canaries; require extra telemetry and a stricter fallback rule set before wider rollout.
Default block size for INT8 set to 128 for throughput/quality sweet spot; provide policy to override per-deployment.
Add safety clipping at 99.995th percentile to mitigate rare code-completion artifacts; schedule follow-up to evaluate adaptive clipping thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: FP8 exponent overflow / jitter causing intermittent p99 spikes. Mitigation: add guardrails that disable FP8 on detected rescale instability and route to INT8 fallback.
Risk: Calibration drift in very-long lived streams. Mitigation: periodic re-calibration checkpoint and telemetry to detect drift beyond 5% variance.
Risk: Edge-case token artifacts for code/completion. Mitigation: tighten clipping for layers identified in failure runs and add prompt-type based gating.
next_steps: Finish full matrix sweep for block sizes {64,128,256} across sequence lengths up to 16k and produce a CSV of results (due 2025-03-12).
Implement runtime rollout hooks and telemetry keys for FP8 experimental flag (PR target 2025-03-08).
Add an automated fuzz-test harness for quantization clipping jitter to reproduce p99 spikes (owner: Riley Gomez).
Schedule a review with Applied ML and Runtime teams to finalize default profile and fallback policy (meeting 2025-03-10).
